title: Greed, Gambling, and Godliness
speaker: Elder Nick Anderson

outline.title: The Prevalence of Gambling in Modern Culture
subpoints: Gambling has become ubiquitous in media and daily life.
Statistics show a significant portion of adults participate in gambling.
The Super Bowl represents the largest single gambling event globally.

outline.title: Godliness with Contentment is Great Gain
subpoints: True gain is found in spiritual contentment, not material wealth.
Believers are called to be satisfied with food and clothing.
The desire to be rich leads to temptation, snares, and destruction.

outline.title: Reasons Why Gambling is Unwise for Christians
subpoints: The Bible commends diligent work over quick riches.
Believers are commanded to plan wisely and manage resources responsibly.
Gambling contradicts the principle of good stewardship of God-given resources.

summary:
In this sermon, Elder Nick Anderson addresses the growing prevalence of gambling in modern culture, noting its prominence during events like the Super Bowl. Using 1 Timothy 6:6-19 as the primary text, he contrasts the worldly pursuit of wealth through gambling with the biblical call to godliness and contentment. The message emphasizes that while the Bible does not explicitly forbid gambling, it provides clear principles regarding money, work, and stewardship that make gambling incompatible with a faithful Christian life.

The speaker outlines several reasons why gambling is unwise, beginning with the biblical commendation of diligent labor over the pursuit of quick riches. Citing Proverbs, he argues that work is a divine command and a path to satisfaction, whereas gambling relies on chance and fosters a lack of understanding. Furthermore, he highlights the importance of wise planning and stewardship, arguing that gambling is an irresponsible use of resources entrusted to believers by God.

The sermon concludes with a call to repentance for those who gamble with the motive of becoming rich, warning that the love of money is a root of evil that can lead to spiritual destruction. Believers are urged to flee from such temptations and instead pursue righteousness, godliness, and faith, trusting in the living God who provides richly for all needs.
